subject: GitHub Copilot's metered cost model and the routing decision of when to spend it

evals.prompt: Define what this skill teaches in 2-3 sentences: Copilot's two cost surfaces (always-free completions vs metered chat/agent), its current billing unit, and when its metered budget is worth spending.
evals.negative_expectation: Must NOT describe Copilot as a model or as unlimited because it is a paid subscription.

evals.prompt: Explain Copilot's post-June-1-2026 billing: GitHub AI Credits (1 credit = $0.01), how cost is computed from tokens, what changed from the legacy premium-request multipliers, and what stays always-free.
evals.negative_expectation: Must NOT claim per-model multipliers still govern general cost post-June-2026, nor that completions are credit-billed.

evals.prompt: Why have an explicit rule for when to spend Copilot's metered budget — what property of the allowance makes spending it on boilerplate pure waste?
evals.negative_expectation: Must NOT ignore the no-rollover / finite-allowance property that makes the waste real.

evals.prompt: Distinguish the `github-copilot` skill from `opencode`, `opencode-free-models`, and `autonomous-loop-patterns`. Name the mechanism each owns.
evals.negative_expectation: Must NOT claim this skill owns the OpenCode runtime, free-model selection, or agent-loop authoring.

evals.prompt: You have an agentic multi-file refactor and, separately, a batch of repetitive formatting edits. You are on Copilot Pro (≈300/month, no rollover). Route each and justify the choice in terms of the metered budget.
evals.negative_expectation: Must NOT spend metered Copilot budget on the repetitive formatting edits when a free/cheap lane or script suffices.

evals.prompt: Classify these as always-free Copilot surface, metered Copilot surface, or 'route off Copilot': inline completions, next-edit suggestions, frontier-model agent refactor, bulk classification of 5000 docs, a deterministic rename across 40 files.
Correct this statement: 'I pay for Copilot Pro+, so running agent flows all day costs me nothing extra and the old request multipliers tell me the cost.'
evals.negative_expectation: Must NOT accept that a subscription makes metered agent flows free, nor that legacy multipliers govern current cost.

evals.prompt: Give an analogy that captures the always-free surface vs the metered, non-rolling allowance, and why you only take the metered lane when the work earns it.
